units.function: Large service-level suite for workspace config, delivery proof, close readiness, safe terminal reaping, branch reconciliation/quarantine recovery, runtime-service projection, reuse summaries and bounded company overview.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> execution-workspace/issue/runtime services -> Drizzle/PostgreSQL + real temporary Git repositories/worktrees + local processes; pull-request detail lookup is injected, while authorization routes and external hosting APIs are outside this unit.
units.keyDataModels: ExecutionWorkspace, ProjectWorkspace, Work/issue tree and execution state, heartbeat Run, WorkProduct/PR, RecoveryAction, comment/reference mention, runtime service, delivery/readiness state, Git inspection/fingerprint/rescue ref and persisted command/environment/runtime config.
units.lifecycle: Resolve config and delivery -> inspect Git/Work/Run/runtime state -> expose bounded readiness/overview -> reconcile safe branch drift or quarantine dirty work -> resolve recovery and restore Work workflow -> sweep only terminal delivered inactive workspaces with revalidation and Git locks -> archive/remove runtime-created assets.
units.testAssessment: The suite contains 43 detailed cases with strong negative, race, recovery and scale scenarios. Sandboxed and approved unsandboxed focused Vitest each passed 8 pure tests and skipped all 35 embedded-Postgres cases, so database/Git/runtime integration claims remain source-inspected but unexecuted on this host.
units.designRationale: Treat a workspace as recoverable operational state rather than a directory: prove delivery precisely, avoid deleting uncertain or newer work, separate shared session archival from infrastructure deletion, fingerprint incoherence, preserve dirty work in rescue refs and serialize repair against lifecycle/runtime changes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral execution workspace/artifact lifecycle that can prove result delivery, preserve evidence, recover safely from drift and cleanup without losing company data, while tying every repair/destructive action to a human responsibility and authorization chain.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT this as the leading reference for code-workspace safety: delivery evidence matching, dirty/newer-work vetoes, pre/post revalidation, Git locking, non-destructive rescue, claimant/runtime race gates, bounded projections and large-volume regression. Place it behind WorkspacePort/ArtifactEvidencePort, generalize delivery beyond GitHub/code, use company-scoped relational integrity and bind every cleanup/repair to an approved ActionGrant and immutable evidence/outbox.
units.responsibilityConflict: Recovery actors are generic board users and operational comments; there is no accountable-human eligibility, Approval decision, ResponsibilityContract, DataAuthorization or exact Action digest. Git mutations, database recovery rows/comments and route-level wakeup/activity cannot be one transaction, yet partial-failure compensation and evidence finality are not demonstrated.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 8/8 pure passed, 35/35 embedded-Postgres skipped
2026-08-19 approved unsandboxed focused Vitest: 8/8 pure passed, 35/35 embedded-Postgres skipped
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL privileged-command surface if reused directly: persisted workspace config carries arbitrary provision/runtime/teardown/cleanup commands and host paths without authority/provenance tests. HIGH transaction boundary: Git deletion/rescue, database state, comments/activity and wakeup cannot be atomic and crash compensation is untested. HIGH ownership-integrity gap: a workspace can reference another company's project at schema level and is only excluded by service query logic. HIGH responsibility gap: destructive repair lacks tested accountable-human approval and exact action digest. HIGH data-governance gap: workspace files, service URLs and paths have no classification/export contract. MEDIUM evidence portability: absolute paths enter fingerprints. MEDIUM verification gap: all 35 integration tests skipped locally.
